title: dynamic-granular-prefill-windows-and-decode-hint-propagation
author: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Production workloads show a tension between large prefill chunks (better kernel throughput and KV cache locality) and small decode latencies required by interactive applications. Previously we used a fixed chunk sizing heuristic and admitted whole-request prefill windows which either increased tail latency or underutilized kernels for short sequences. This PR introduces an adaptive, micro-window based prefill system plus a lightweight decode-hint propagation mechanism so downstream scheduler and kernel selection can make more informed decisions.

Design highlights: 1) Dynamic prefill windowing: requests are partitioned into micro-prefill windows (configurable min/max token ranges) based on observed sequence length distribution and live queue pressure. Windows can be merged opportunistically when KV cache locality and kernel throughput favor batching. 2) Decode hint propagation: prefill stage emits compact hints (estimated logits-span, kv-warmth, expected remaining tokens) attached to request metadata. Scheduler and kernel selector use these to: prioritize low-latency decode kernels for short-remaining requests, co-locate windows with high KV-warmth, and avoid heavy kernel launches for tiny decodes. Hints are intentionally small (one 12-byte struct) to avoid serialization overhead. 3) Scheduler changes: stream_quota allocator extended to support per-window weights; admission controller applies a micro-window backpressure when the decode queue is saturated. 4) KV cache warmup: warmup sampler triggers early KV prefetch for windows predicted to reuse cache and defers prefetch for ephemeral micro-windows. 5) Continuous batching integration: micro-windows can be appended to in-flight batches if their hint indicates compatible shape (sequence length bucket and kv-warmth), improving kernel occupancy without blocking latency-sensitive decodes.

Implementation summary: high-level files modified: runtime/prefill/window_manager.cpp (core algorithm), runtime/scheduler/stream_quotas.cpp (allocator), runtime/kernels/decode_hint.cpp (hint type + selector hooks), runtime/kv_cache/warmup.cc (prefetch policy), runtime/batching/continuous_batcher.cpp (micro-window append path), docs/ops/prefill_windows.md (operator runbook), tests/e2e/prefill_integration_test.py (integration harness). Key algorithmic points are implemented with conservative defaults and feature flags (feature.dynamic_prefill=true, feature.decode_hints=true) to allow staged rollout.

Checklist: - [x] Algorithm and design docs updated - [x] Unit tests for window manager and hint propagation - [x] E2E benchmark showing improved p95 for mixed workloads - [x] Feature-flag gated rollout and metrics emitted - [x] Ops runbook added for tuning thresholds

Commits: small, focused commits with clear messages are included in the PR (see commits field).

Testing & results: Microbench harness (mixed interactive: 60% short requests <32 tokens, 40% long prefill requests) shows: p50 latency: -2ms (stable), p95 latency: -18% (from 124ms to 102ms) for interactive requests; tail decode latency improved by 25% when micro-windows were allowed to bypass large-kernel queues. Throughput: sustained tokens/sec for long batches unchanged within +/-3%. KV cache hit-rate improved ~4% on workloads with repeated short prefixes. All numbers are median of five runs on identical 8xA100 nodes with the standard benchmark-lab harness.

Rollout plan: ship behind feature flags, enable for 10% traffic for 48h, monitor p95 and KV hit metrics, then 50% for 24h, full rollout if no regressions.

Migration and compatibility: hints are optional and backward-compatible; kernel selector falls back to previous heuristics when decode_hints is absent. No customer-facing API changes.

Related: references ENG-3241 (prefill window tuning) and ENG-3377 (kv warmup improvements).

Notes on CI: initial e2e run surfaced a flaky test in continuous_batcher append path under extreme scheduling races. Fixed by adding a lightweight CAS in continuous_batcher (commit 0003) and an extra unit test that repros the race while keeping performance impact minimal.
commits: 0001/introduce-dynamic-prefill-window-manager: add adaptive windowing core and APIs
0002/decode-hints: emit compact hint struct alongside prefill responses and plumb to scheduler
0003/continuous-batcher-cas-fix: race fix for append path, add unit repro
0004/kv-warmup-policy: sampler-based early prefetch and deferral heuristics
0005/docs-and-tests: ops runbook and e2e integration tests + benchmark configs
review_comments: Samir Patel: Left a few suggestions around the weight calculation in stream_quotas.cpp — prefer using exponential smoothing for short-lived streams. Also asked for a comment on fallback behavior when hints are missing.
Maya Chen (author): Addressed smoothing suggestion in commit 0003 and added explicit fallback paths documented in window_manager.h. Added a unit test covering missing-hint flows.

Ava Rodríguez: Noted that the KV prefetch threshold might overfetch in degenerate prefix-heavy workloads; suggested adding a max-prefetch budget per stream. Implemented as a configurable knob with sane defaults.
Jonas Müller: Approved after verifying no regression in existing scheduler benchmarks and after CI green. Recommended adding a brief note in ops runbook about tuning micro-window merge thresholds.
release_notes: Introduce dynamic micro-prefill windows and decode hint propagation to reduce decode tail latency for mixed interactive workloads. Feature-flagged and configurable. No breaking changes.
performance_summary: Mixed workload: interactive p95 -18% (124ms -> 102ms), tail decode latency -25% in stress cases, throughput +/-3%, KV hit-rate +4%.
notes: Feature gated with feature.dynamic_prefill and feature.decode_hints. Ops runbook contains tuning guidance. CI initially failed due to a race; fixed in follow-up commit.
